question: Will SRS or DOE have publicly stated a cause for the October 28, 2026 Savannah River National Laboratory fire by November 13, 2026?

calls.reasoning: Status quo after 6 days: no cause stated. SRS/DOE have been tight-lipped, saying nothing about the room, the material or how the fire was put out, and said only that an investigation is underway; such investigations typically take weeks to months. The radiological-release reversal makes the site more cautious about what it says, not less. On the other side, media and political pressure is strong (CNN, Fox, Newsweek coverage) and an employee was injured, so SRNS or DOE might give reporters a preliminary or suspected cause (for example an electrical or equipment fault), and the bar is low: 'suspected cause' counts. But 10 days remain and the next public forum, the Citizens Advisory Board meeting on Nov 17, falls after the deadline. No market found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.

The only on-the-record comment is DOE EM's Oct 29 statement that an investigation is underway, and they have not even named the room or the material. The site is defensive after reversing its account of a radiological release, and the next public forum, the CAB meeting on Nov 17, falls after the deadline. On the other side, media and watchdog pressure is heavy and 'suspected/preliminary cause' counts, so an offhand comment such as 'electrical fault' or 'equipment malfunction' to local press is a real tail. calls.reconciliation: The three runs agree on every checkable fact: three SRS releases, all dated Oct 28, with no cause given; DOE EM's Volk saying on Oct 29 that an investigation is underway; nothing new after Oct 31; the CAB meeting on Nov 17 falling after the window; and no market. No factual disputes needed settling, and I had no web access on this run. The only difference is judgment, 0.13 versus 0.14. I land slightly lower than all three for two reasons: a Site Area Emergency classification makes a formal DOE investigation likely, and formal investigations usually hold back preliminary causal statements; the site has also gone quiet since its release reversal. More than a third of the window has passed with silence.
